pool.text: Puri Pemecutan palace was destroyed in a fire during the Dutch intervention in Bali.
The royal palace in Denpasar was looted and razed during the Dutch intervention.
Pura Maospahit Hindu temple was heavily damaged by the Bali earthquake and rebuilt afterward.
The port located about 10 km from the city center has been operating since this year.
Tuban Airfield, now part of Denpasar International Airport, officially opened.
Tuban Airfield was seized by the Imperial Japanese forces during World War II.
Denpasar officially became the seat of government for the province of Bali.
Act No. 1 officially established the City of Denpasar as an autonomous city.
Foreign tourists visiting Denpasar reached 1,413,513 people, led by visitors from Japan.
Sarbagita was made official by Presidential Regulation Number 45 covering the tourist regions.
The city started operating a bus rapid transit system called Trans Sarbagita.
An average of 2,800 passengers per day used the Trans Sarbagita service.
Two major improvements to the road system in Denpasar were completed.
Denpasar achieved among the fastest growth in tourism globally alongside Jakarta and Batam.
The central government initiated another transport system called Trans Metro Dewata.
